title: Install daybook: shift handoff + customer blockers (Nov 3-5, 2026)
body:
Summary
- This is a daybook style handoff covering the Nov 3 to Nov 5 install window for two active on-prem customers. Primary focus: Nebula Health (air-gapped onprem) and Acero Finance (VPC w/ strict egress policy).
- Main themes: unresolved KMS integration, intermittent MTU mismatch causing RPC failures, and a model-serving performance regression on Nebula after quantization flip.

Attendees (rotating shifts)
- Day shift owners: Ava Martinez, Daniel Kim
- Night shift owners: Priya Shah, Miguel Alvarez
- Escalation oncall: Sanjay Rao
- Customer POCs: Elena (Nebula infra lead), Raj (Acero SRE)

Daily log highlights
2026-11-03 (init day)
- Morning sync 09:00 PT: validated hardware inventory at Nebula site: 3 x A100 40GB, tock BIOS v1.2, Ubuntu 22.04 image.
- Preflight found 2 items: missing HSM cert chain that KMS expects, and switch MTU default at 1400 in edge router (we expect 9000).
- Action: Daniel uploaded temporary KMS shim that accepts unsigned certs for staging 10.0.2.0/24. Patch ref PD-2891.
- Blocking note: Customer security team will not proceed with shim in prod until HSM vendor provides cert chain. Customer asked for detailed mitigation plan.

2026-11-04 (day 2)
- Morning runbook tabletop with Nebula and Redwood SecOps at 08:30 PT. Decision: proceed with network-only validation using internal test model that excludes PII.
- Observed: inference P50 latency with default quantized weights is 62 ms token, target 18-22 ms. Investigation shows kernel falling back to slower GEMM path after quantization flag flip.
- Hypothesis: compilation selected float path due to per-layer dtype mismatch introduced by the customer's pinned cuBLAS 12.1.3 driver.
- Temporary workaround: switch to mixed-int8 profile and enable continuous batching = off for small requests. This brings median to ~28 ms but increases GPU utilization 18%.
- Action: Miguel to open INF-4321 with kernel trace, attach perf profile and environment matrix.
- Blocking note: Acero Finance reported intermittent gRPC TLS handshake failures inside their VPC when cross-subnet calls exceed 120 concurrent streams. Suspect NAT ephemeral port exhaustion.

2026-11-05 (handoff update)
- Night prep 20:00 PT: applied network fix on Acero side - reduced ephemeral port reuse timeout and added SNAT pool per node. Early signs show TLS failure rate dropped by 90%.
- Nebula: HSM vendor delivered cert bundle but it fails the chain-of-trust check due to a missing intermediate. SecOps requested vendor to reissue with correct intermediate; ETA 48 hours.
- Customer acceptance testing: Ran 1k sample inferences through private deploy proxy; correctness checksum passed, but tail latency spikes at 500 ms on 0.1% of requests. Likely related to GC pauses in user workload on host.

Decisions and tradeoffs
- Do not merge KMS shim to customer prod; maintain shim on staging only. Rationale: security posture and customer compliance.
- Prioritize kernel/driver compatibility workstream over speculative quantization rewrites. Short-term lift yields better latency gains with less risk.

Open blockers (priority list)
1) Nebula HSM intermediate cert missing - blocks full KMS integration and prod signoff. Owner: Elena (customer) / Sanjay (redwood outreach). ETA: customer/vendor 48-72 hours.
2) Kernel fallback after quantization on Nebula due to cublas abi mismatch - blocks stable latency SLO. Owner: Miguel. Action item: repro with pinned driver 12.1.3 and attach perf traces to INF-4321. ETA: 3 business days.
3) Acero VPC TLS handshake failures during high concurrent streams - mitigated but needs confirmation under load. Owner: Daniel. Action: run synthetic 10k concurrent stream test in staging. ETA: 24 hours.
4) Host-level GC tail spikes on Nebula test VM - investigate whether user workload cron jobs coincide with spikes. Owner: Priya. Action: enable pidstat and perf sampling for 48 hours. ETA: 48 hours.

Action items (owner, what, due)
- Miguel Alvarez: assemble kernel traces, open PR with adjusted compilation flags for mixed-int8 fallback, link to INF-4321. Due 2026-11-06.
- Daniel Kim: run Acero 10k concurrency staging test and collect network telemetry. Due 2026-11-06 morning.
- Priya Shah: instrument Nebula hosts with lightweight sampler and correlate cron schedule. Due 2026-11-07.
- Sanjay Rao: coordinate with Nebula security and vendor to get proper intermediate cert and update runbook. Due 2026-11-07.
- Ava Martinez: prepare customer-facing status note for Nebula and Acero summarizing risks and temporary mitigations. Due 2026-11-05 EOD.

Notes / context pointers
- Runbook: link in linked_artifacts for Nebula onprem runbook. Follow the section KMS-integration -> fallback modes.
- Related PR: github PR 614 contains the shim code and test harness. Do not merge to main.
- Jira: INF-4321 contains the perf traces. PD-2891 is staffing/shift roster for install window.

Meeting threads and follow-ups
- Internal: slack thread 'install-nebula' has live logs and the ssh bastion debug output. Keep channel pinned for night shift.
- Customer sync: scheduled 2026-11-06 09:00 PT for acceptance gate review. Please have kernel traces and telemetry attached before the meeting.

Retro / quick learnings
- For air-gapped installs, require vendor cert chain verification as part of preflight checklist; avoid ad-hoc shims that create compliance tangles.
- Add driver ABI matrix to onboarding checklist: which cuBLAS/cuDNN versions are compatible with each quantization profile.

Appendix: quick debugging commands used during shifts
- capture kernel trace: /opt/redwood/bin/trace-kernel --pid 1223 --duration 30s > /tmp/kernel_trace_11-04.pb
- check MTU path: sudo ip link show && sudo ethtool -k eth0
- validate KMS handshake: openssl s_client -connect 10.0.2.5:443 -CAfile /etc/redwood/kms/ca.pem -showcerts

If you pick up tonight's shift, please start with the last 30 minutes of the slack 'install-nebula' channel and the trace in /tmp starting with kernel_trace_11-04.pb. Escalate to Sanjay if the HSM vendor reply is still incomplete.
